Fragmenta in epistulam ad Ephesios (in catenis)
Eph: Prolog
Ὥσπερ τοῖς Ῥωμαίοις ἔγραφεν, ὅτε μηδέπω αὐτοὺς τεθέατο, οὕτω καὶ τοῖς
Ἐφεσίοις, Ἰωάννου προλαβόντος καὶ τὸ κήρυγμα αὐτοῖς καταβαλλομένου, εὐκαίρως
παραινῶν αὐτοῖς μὴ κρατεῖσθαι νόμῳ. ἐπειδὴ οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις
διάγοντες διὰ τοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς περιτομῆς πιστεύσαντας ἐτήρουν νόμον, εἶτα ἐπειδὴ
ἱκανῶς ὁ Ἰωάννης ἐθεολόγησε καὶ οὐδὲν ἐνέλιπε τῶν εἰς θεογνωσίαν κηρυγμάτων,
ὡς ἦν ἀνθρώποις χωρητόν, ἐπὶ τὸ παραστῆσαι τῆς ἐνανθρωπήσεως τὴν οἰκονομίαν,
ἔρχεται τὸ οἰκεῖον αὐτῇ μέγεθος καὶ διὰ ῥημάτων ἀξίως τῶν πραγμάτων 305
περιτιθεὶς καὶ τὸ δυσκολώτερον ἀναδεξάμενος· τὸ μὲν γὰρ τῆς θεότητος εἶχεν
οἰκεῖον τὸ ἀξίωμα καὶ ὡμολογημένον, τὸ δὲ τῆς ἐνανθρωπήσεως κατὰ τὸ
φαινόμενον ταπεινὸν ἀξίως διηγήσασθαι δυνάμεως ἦν πνευματικῆς. Eph 1,1
Κἀνταῦθα τὸ διὰ καὶ τῷ θεῷ προσήκει κατὰ τὸν Παῦλον, καὶ οὐκ ἠλάττωται πατήρ.
εἰκότως δὲ λέγει τὸ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ, ἵνα δείξῃ ὅτι ὡς ἠθέλησεν ὁ θεὸς Ἰωάννην
εἶναι ἀπόστολον οὕτως κἀμέ. τοῦτο δὲ γράφει, ἵνα ἀξιόπιστα ᾖ τὰ ὑπ' αὐτοῦ
λεγόμενα. Eph 1,2 Εἰ ἑκάτερον καταχρηστικῶς εἴρηται, καὶ τὸ πατὴρ καὶ τὸ κύριος,
ὁμολογηθήσεται μείζων τοῦ πατρὸς ὁ υἱός, εἰ ὁ μὲν πατρὸς ἔχει ὄνομα, ὁ δὲ κυρίου.
ἀλλ' ὡμολόγηται τούτων τῶν ῥητῶν ἡ αἰτία· ἐπειδὴ γὰρ εἶπεν· πατρὸς ἡμῶν, πατὴρ
δέ ἐστι τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἵνα μὴ τὸ αὐτὸ ὄνομα καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ μονογενοῦς καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν
πιστῶν ᾖ κείμενον, ἢ τὸν υἱὸν καθελῇ παρὰ φύσιν, ἢ ἐκείνους ὑπὲρ φύσιν ἀναγάγῃ,
εἰπὼν πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ δεικνὺς ὅτι χάριτι ἡ προσηγορία, ἐπήγαγεν· καὶ κυρίου
Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· οὐ γὰρ ἐνῆν κοινῇ φύσει τῆς προσηγορίας οὔσης κοινὸν εἶναι καὶ τὸ
ἀξίωμα. διὰ τί οὖν κύριος μὲν τούτων ὁ πατήρ, οὐχὶ δὲ καὶ αὐτὸς κύριος τοῦ υἱοῦ,
εἴπερ καταχρηστικὸν ἦν τὸ τῆς προσηγορίας ἐφ' ἑκατέρων; Eph 1,4 Εἰ τοίνυν ἐν
Χριστῷ εἰς υἱοθεσίαν ὡρίσθησαν οἱ ἅγιοι, οὐ θετὸς ὁ υἱός, ἀλλὰ φύσει υἱός. Eph 1,5–
6 Εἰ κατὰ τὸν νόμον ἡ θέλησις ἐνέργειά ἐστιν, τίς ἡ εὐδοκία ἡ ταύτης τῆς θελήσεως;
οὐ γὰρ ἂν εἶπε «θέλησιν θελήματος». Εἰς ἔπαινον δόξης τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ.
προλαβὼν ἤδη εἶπον ὅτι κατακοσμεῖ τὸν ἑαυτοῦ λόγον τῷ ἀξιώματι τῆς οἰκονομίας.
306 Eph 1,10 Ἐπειδὴ ἔπεσεν ὁ πλασθεὶς διὰ τῆς παρακοῆς, καὶ ἀσεβησάντων τῶν
ἀνθρώπων ἀπηλλοτριώθη τὰ ἐπουράνια τῶν ἐπιγείων, ἐλθὼν ὁ Χριστὸς πάντα
ἀνεκεφαλαιώσατο. καὶ τοῦτο μετὰ ταῦτα ἑτέρως φησὶν εἰπών· εἰρηνοποιήσας τὰ ἐν
τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καὶ τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς. αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ἡ εἰρήνη ἡμῶν, ὁ ποιήσας τὰ
ἀμφότερα ἕν, τοὺς Ἰουδαίους καὶ τοὺς Ἕλληνας, διὰ τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν πίστεως. Eph
1,11 Φανερῶς ἐνταῦθα ἄλλο ἐνέργειαν λέγει καὶ ἄλλο βούλησιν. εἰπὼν τοῦ τὰ πάντα
ἐνεργοῦντος κατὰ τὴν βουλήν, εἶπεν τοῦ θελήματος, ἵνα δείξῃ κεκριμένον τὸ
θέλημα. ἅπερ ἄν τις ἀπὸ βουλῆς καλῆς ἐβεβαίωσεν, ταῦτα κρίσει ὥρισται, λέγων
ἐχρήσατο ταῖς φωναῖς. Eph 1,13 Τῶν προεγνωσμένων, φησίν, ἐστὲ καὶ ὑμεῖς,
οἰκειούμενοι Χριστῷ δι' ὑπακοῆς καὶ τῆς ἐπὶ τῇ ἀκοῇ πίστεως καὶ τοῦ ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει
σφραγισμοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν ὁμοίωσις πρὸς Χριστὸν διὰ τῆς τοῦ πνεύματος μεταλήψεως.
παρὰ τίνος δὲ ἤκουσαν τὸν λόγον τῆς ἀληθείας; ἢ παρὰ Ἰωάννου τοῦ εὐαγγελιστοῦ;
ἐκεῖ γὰρ ἐκήρυττεν. διὸ καὶ ὑψηλότερον αὐτοῖς ὁ Παῦλος διαλέγεται ἐκ τῆς ἐκείνου
διδασκαλίας κατηρτισμένοις. Eph 1,14.17–21 Ἡ ἀπολύτρωσις τῆς περιποιήσεώς
ἐστιν· ἵνα γὰρ περιποιηθῶμεν καὶ οἰκειωθῶμεν τῷ θεῷ, ἀπολυτρούμεθα,
μεμνημένοι δὲ τοῦ αἵματος οὗ ἀπελυτρώθημεν καὶ τῆς οἰκονομίας πάσης. φανερὸν
ὅτι θεὸν τὸ κατὰ σάρκα τοῦ Χριστοῦ λέγει· οὐδαμοῦ γὰρ ἐνταῦθα τοῦ τῆς θεότητος
ἀξιώματος ἐμνημόνευσεν, ἀλλὰ τῆς καθ' ἡμᾶς οἰκονομίας ἥτις ὡμολόγηται τῆς
σαρκὸς εἶναι. δόξαν δὲ πολλάκις ἡ γραφὴ λέγει αὐτὴν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν οὐσίαν· ἐπειδὴ
english: Just as he wrote to the Romans before he had seen them, so also to the Ephesians, after John had preceded and cast the preaching to them, timely exhorting them not to be mastered by the law. Since the apostles, passing through Jerusalem, kept the law because of those who believed from the circumcision, and then since John had sufficiently theologized and left nothing of the preachings toward the knowledge of God, as was capable for men, in order to present the economy of the incarnation, there comes the appropriate magnitude and, through words worthy of the things, being set forth and having taken up the more difficult matter: for the divinity had an appropriate and confessed honor, but the incarnation, according to appearances humble, was able to narrate worthily by spiritual power.

And thus 'through' and 'to God' according to Paul, and it is not diminished, Father (Eph 1:1). And rightly he says 'through the will of God', so that he might show that just as God willed John to be an apostle, so also we. And he writes this so that the things said by him might be trustworthy.

If each has been used appropriately, both Father and Lord, the Son will be confessed greater than the Father, if the one has the name Father, and the other Lord (Eph 1:2). But the cause of these sayings was confessed: because he said, 'our Father', and [He] is Father of Christ, so that the same name might not be placed also upon the only-begotten and upon the believers, or else he would cast down the Son against nature, or lift those up above nature, having said 'our Father' and showing that the appellation is by grace, he brought forward: and 'Lord Jesus Christ'; for it was not in common nature, since the appellation not being common, the honor was not to be common. Why then is the Father Lord of these, but he himself is not also Lord of the Son, if the appellation of both was used appropriately?
If then in Christ for adoption (Eph 1:4)...

The saints were defined; the Son is not merely appointed, but Son by nature. Regarding Eph 1:5–6, if according to the law the will is an activity, what is this good pleasure of that will? For he would not have said 'the will of a will.' It is for the praise of the glory of his grace. Having already spoken beforehand, he said that he orders his own Word by the requirement of the economy.

Regarding Eph 1:10: Because the created [being] fell through disobedience, and because men acted impiously, the heavenly things were alienated from the earthly; Christ having come, he recapitulated all things. And after this, he says something differently: having made peace between those in the heavens and those on the earth. For he himself is our peace, the one who made both the two into one, the Jews and the Greeks, through the faith into Christ. Regarding Eph 1:11: Clearly here he says one thing for 'activity' and another for 'will.' Having spoken of the one working all things according to the will, he spoke of the will, in order to show that the will is decreed. Whatever anyone has established from a good purpose, these things are decreed to judge, saying he used the voices. Regarding Eph 1:13: Of those foreknown, he says, you also are, being made ones with Christ through obedience and through the faith that comes by hearing and the seal that comes by faith, which is a likeness to Christ through the appropriation of the Spirit. But from whom did they hear the word of truth? Or from John the Evangelist? For there he was preaching. Therefore, Paul discourses with them on a higher level, having been equipped from that [teaching].

Regarding Eph 1:14, 17–21: The redemption of the possession is this; for we are redeemed so that we might be possessed and made at home with God, being redeemed, remembering the blood by which we were redeemed and the whole economy. It is clear that he calls the one according to the flesh of Christ 'God'; for nowhere here does he mention the requirement of divinity, but the economy toward us, which confesses that the flesh is [real]. Yet often the Scripture calls that very essence of God 'glory'; because...

γὰρ ἀψηλάφητος καὶ ἀνέφικτος, δόξαν αὐτὴν ὠνόμασεν ἵνα μὴ λόγον ἀπαιτῇς ἀλλὰ
προσκυνῇς. πρῶτος τὴν οὐσίαν τοῦ θεοῦ δόξαν λέγει Ἰεζεκιὴλ ἐν ὀπτασίαις
θεασάμενος τὸν θεὸν καθεζόμενον, καὶ ἐπάγων· τοῦτο ὁμοίωμα τῆς δόξης κυρίου.
ὅπερ ἀλλαχοῦ ἑρμηνεύων ὁ θεός φησιν· ἐγὼ ὁράσεις ἐπλήθυνα 307 καὶ ἐν χερσὶ
προφητῶν ὡμοιώθην. ἣν οὖν εἶπε δόξαν ὁ Ἰεζεκιήλ, ταύτην ὁ θεός φησι τὸ ἐγώ.
λέγει δὲ Παῦλος· ὃς ὢν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς δόξης–ποίας δόξης; –καὶ χαρακτὴρ τῆς
ὑποστάσεως αὐτοῦ. κἀνταῦθα τοίνυν τὸ μὲν θεὸς τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
κατὰ τὴν σάρκα λέγει, τὸ δὲ πατὴρ τῆς δόξης κατὰ τὴν φύσιν. Καὶ παντὸς ὀνόματος
ὀνομαζομένου οὐ μόνον ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι. ἐν γὰρ τῷ
αἰῶνι τούτῳ ὀνομάζομεν θρόνους, ἀρχάς, κυριότητας, ἐξουσίας, δυνάμεις, ἀγγέλους,
ἀρχαγγέλους· ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἔστι μυρία τάγματα ἀοράτων δυνάμεων ἡμῖν ἄγνωστα καὶ
διὰ τοῦτο ἀκατονόμαστα, μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἔσται γνωστὰ καὶ λήψεται μετὰ τῆς
γνώσεως καὶ τὴν παρ' ἡμῶν προσηγορίαν, διὰ τοῦτο εἶπεν· καὶ ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι. Eph
1,22–23 Καὶ αὐτὸν ἔδωκε κεφαλὴν ὑπὲρ πάντων τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἥτις ἐστὶ τὸ σῶμα
αὐτοῦ, τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι πληρουμένου. διὰ τούτου ἐδήλωσεν ὅτι
πλήρωμα τοῦ θεοῦ λέγει τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὴν ἐκκλησίαν. διὰ τί δὲ
πλήρωμα; ἐπειδὴ πεπλήρωται θεοῦ· ὥσπερ γάρ, φησίν, ἐν πᾶσι τὰ πάντα πληροῖ,
οὕτως καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ πληροῦται κατὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτὴν σῶμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
Χριστοῦ οὖν σῶμα, πλήρωμα δὲ θεοῦ ἡ ἐκκλησία. Τοῦ τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσι
πληρουμένου. ἔστι γὰρ ἐν οὐρανῷ, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἐνεργῶν οὐχ ὡς ἐν γῇ, καὶ ἔστιν ἐν
γῇ, οὐχ ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ ἐνεργῶν, καὶ ἐν ἀγγέλοις, ἐν ἡλίῳ, ἀλλ' ἐν ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν
αὐτοῦ φύσιν· λέγει γὰρ ἀφ' ὧν μεταλαμβάνομεν ἡ γραφὴ περὶ θεοῦ, οὐκ ἀφ' ὧν
αὐτός ἐστιν· τοῦτο γὰρ ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστιν. Eph 2,2–3 Κόσμος διττῶς λέγεται, καὶ ἡ
σύστασις ἡ δημιουργικὴ καὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸ σύστημα τὸ πονηρόν. νυνὶ δὲ διεῖλε
τοῖς ἀνόμοις τὰ πράγματα, αἰῶνα καλέσας τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὴν πονηρίαν καὶ τὴν
ἁμαρτίαν, κόσμον δὲ τὴν σύστησιν τοῦ παντός, καθὼς καὶ ἐν τῇ πρὸς Γαλάτας λέγει·
ὅπως ἐξέληται ἡμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος αἰῶνος πονηροῦ. τοῦτον τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα λέγει.
τὴν οὖν κοινὴν 308 ἀπόστασιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ πλάνην αἰῶνα ὠνόμασεν, ἧς
μέρος ἦσαν ποτὲ καὶ οἱ νῦν πιστεύσαντες τῷ Χριστῷ. Κατὰ τὸν ἄρχοντα τῆς ἐξουσίας
τοῦ ἀέρος τοῦ πνεύματος. φανερῶς διὰ τούτου δείκνυσιν ὁ ἀπόστολος, ὅτι οὐκ ἀπ'
οὐρανοῦ ἄγγελος ἦν ὁ διάβολος, ἀλλ' ἀέριόν τι πονηρὸν πνεῦμα. κἂν ὁ κύριος λέγῃ·
εἶδον τὸν σατανᾶν ὡς ἀστραπὴν πεσόντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, οὐχὶ τὸν τόπον δείκνυσιν
ὅθεν ἔπεσεν, ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ ἄνωθεν ἡ ἀστραπὴ ὀξέως πίπτει, τὴν ὀξύτητα τῆς
διαβολικῆς πτώσεως ἀστραπῇ παρέβαλε λέγων· ὡς ἀστραπὴ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ὀξέως
φέρεται, οὕτως εἶδον τὴν πτῶσιν αὐτοῦ ὀξεῖαν. Τοῦ νῦν ἐνεργοῦντος. ἐδήλωσεν ὅτι
οὐ πάντοτε τὴν ἰσχὺν ὁ διάβολος ἔχει, ἀλλ' ἡ ἀσθένεια τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἰσχὺς αὐτῷ
γέγονεν. Ποιοῦντες τὰ θελήματα τῆς σαρκὸς καὶ τῶν διανοιῶν. ἐκ τούτου δείκνυται
ὅτι οὐκ ἀντίκειται ἡ σὰρξ τῇ ψυχῇ· συνεφώνει γὰρ εἰς τὴν ἁμαρτίαν. Καὶ ἦμεν τέκνα
φύσει ὀργῆς. ὥσπερ υἱοὶ γεέννης, οὕτω καὶ τέκνα ὀργῆς. Eph 2,10 Ἐπειδὴ εἶπεν
κτισθέντες, λέγει· ἡ κτίσις οἰκείωσίς ἐστιν. τὸ δὲ ἐπὶ ἔργοις ἀγαθοῖς ἐπήγαγεν, ἵνα
λοιπὸν σαυτὸν οἰκοδομῇς. Eph 2,13 Οὐκ εἶπεν «ἐγγύτερον» τῶν πιστευσάντων ἀπὸ
περιτομῆς, ἀλλ' ἐγγύς. Eph 2,14–15α Τὸ μεσότοιχον τοῦ φραγμοῦ λύσας, οὐ τὸν
φραγμόν, ἀλλὰ τὸ μεσότοιχον. τίς δὲ ὁ φραγμός; ἀφελῶ τὸν φραγμὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ
english: For [it is] ungraspable and unreachable; He named this glory so that you would not demand a definition but rather worship. First, Ezekiel calls the essence of God 'glory' after having seen God seated in visions, and he adds: this is the likeness of the Lord's glory. This is what God says He is interpreting elsewhere: 'I will multiply myself and be made like [something] in the hands of prophets.' That which Ezekiel called glory, God says is the 'I am'. And Paul says: 'who is the radiance of His glory'—of what glory?—'and the character of His substance.' Thus, here too, [it is] the God of our Lord Jesus Christ according to the flesh, and the Father of glory according to nature.

And of every name being named, not only in this age but also in the age to come. For in this age we name thrones, principalities, lordships, authorities, powers, angels, archangels; but since there are ten thousand hosts of invisible powers unknown to us and therefore unnamable, after the resurrection they shall be known and shall receive, along with knowledge, also the designation from us; therefore He said: 'and in the age to come.' [Ephesians 1:22–23] And He gave him [as] head over all things to the church, which is His body, the fullness of the [One] filling all things in all. Through this He showed that the body of Christ says [it is] the fullness of God, that is, the church. And why 'fullness'? Because it has been filled by God; for just as, He says, He fills all things in all, so also He is filled in the church according to the fact that it is the body of Christ. Therefore, the church is the body of Christ and the fullness of God. [Of the One] filling all things in all. For He is in heaven, that is, working not as in earth, and He is in earth, not working as in heaven, and in angels, in the sun, but in each according to its own nature; for the Scripture says, concerning those from whom we receive...
Concerning God, not from the things of which He is; for this is incomprehensible. The world is said to be twofold: the creative constitution and the evil system of men.

Now he has distinguished things for the lawless, calling the evil and sin of men an age, and the arrangement of all things a world, just as he says to the Galatians: so that we might be delivered from this present evil age (Galatians 4:5). He speaks of this present age. Thus he named the common apostasy and wandering of men an age, of which even those now having believed in Christ were once a part.

According to the ruler of the authority of the air of the spirit. The apostle clearly demonstrates through this that the devil was not an angel from heaven, but an evil airy spirit. Even if the Lord says: I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven (Luke 10:18), he does not demonstrate the place from which he fell, but because lightning falls sharply from above, he compared the sharpness of the diabolical fall to lightning, saying: just as lightning is carried sharply from heaven, so I saw his sharp fall.

Of the one now working. He made it manifest that the devil does not always have strength, but the weakness of men has become strength to him. Doing the desires of the flesh and of the minds. From this it is shown that the flesh does not oppose the soul; for it agreed toward sin (Ephesians 2:3). And we were children by nature of wrath. Just as sons of hell, so also children of wrath.
Since he said 'having been created' (Ephesians 2:10), he says: the creation is a habitation. And that which led to good works, so that you might build yourself up in the remainder.

He did not say 'nearer' than those believing from the circumcision (Ephesians 2:13), but 'near'. Having broken the middle wall of the partition (Ephesians 2:14), not the partition itself, but the middle wall. And what is the partition? I will take away his partition and

ἔσται εἰς διαρπαγήν, τοῦτ' ἔστι τὴν 309 ἀσφάλειαν τοῦ πνεύματος. τί δὲ τὸ
μεσότοιχον; τὸ πρὸς τοὺς Ἕλληνας ἄμικτον· κεκώλυτο γὰρ Ἕλλησιν ἐπιμίγνυσθαι
Ἰουδαίους, ἵναμὴ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι εἰς τὴν εἰδωλολατρείαν καταπέσωσιν, οἱ καὶ χωρὶς
τούτου εἰδωλολατροῦντες. καὶ τοῦτό ἐστιν ὃ λέγει ∆αυίδ· ὁ θεὸς κατοικίζει
μονοτρόπους ἐν οἴκῳ. ἔδει γὰρ τὸ προζύμιον ἰσχυρὸν γενέσθαι, ἵν' οὕτως τὸ ὅλον
τοῦ κόσμου ζυμωθῇ. Τὸν νόμον τῶν ἐντολῶν τὸν νενομισμένον λέγει, ὡς ἀπὸ τῶν
ἐντολῶν τῶν Μωϋσαϊκῶν. ἐν δόγμασι, τοῖς ἰδίοις, καταργήσας, ὧν ἐστιν· οὐ τὰ
εἰσπορευόμενα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον–τοῦτο δὲ ἔλυεν τὸ τόδε φάγε, τόδε μὴ φάγῃς–,
καὶ τὸ μὴ διδόναι βιβλίον ἀποστασίου–τοῦτο ὑπεναντίως εἶχε πρὸς τὸ κατὰ πᾶσαν
αἰτίαν ἀφιέναι γυναῖκα–, καὶ τὸ ἡμέρας παρατηρεῖσθε καὶ μῆνας καὶ καιροὺς καὶ
ἐνιαυτούς– ἐναντίον ἦν οἷς ἔδωκε Μωϋσῆς. καὶ ὅλως πολλὰ τοιαῦτα ἐστὶ δογματικὰ
οἷς τὸν νόμον τῶν ἐντολῶν κατήργησεν, οὐ τὰς ἐντολὰς ὡς ἀτόπους, ἀλλὰ τὸ ἔθος

english: It will be for plunder, that is, the security of the Spirit. And what is the partition? It is that which is unmixed toward the Greeks; for Jews were forbidden to mingle with Greeks, so that the Jews might not fall into idolatry, they who even apart from this are idolaters. And this is what David says: God dwells in a single way in a house (Ps 68:6). For it was necessary for the leaven to become strong, so that thus the whole of the world might be leavened.

He speaks of the law of commandments, the established one, as being from the Mosaic commandments. By dogmas, by their own [rules], having abolished—which are: not what enters in makes a man common—this [rule] was 'this eat, that do not eat'—and not to give a letter of divorce—this was contrary to the [rule] of dismissing a woman for every cause—and the observing of days and months and seasons and years—it was contrary to those which Moses gave. And in total, many such things are dogmatic, by which he abolished the law of commandments, not the commandments as being out of place, but the custom as no longer being useful. For the commandments are honored even if they do not operate, but the law, therefore, that is, being under the law of commandments among us, harmed after the grace.

For the Greeks indeed are separated from idolatry as impiety, and the Jews from the law as no longer being useful, they are being rebuilt into a certain newness of piety (Eph 2:15b-17). Making peace. For the law does not intend to be peace. Why? So that peace might not stir up bodily war against piety. He will reconcile both to God. Since the Greeks were wandering and the Jews had overstepped. Having killed the enmity in himself. The meaning has breadth in the brevity of the word; for since the law was the one dividing Jews from Greeks according to what was said before, and the law was going to cease, not otherwise...

He breathed [life] because the Lord rose from the dead, to whom it was necessary to unite the church with another man according to the law; he says that in his flesh he killed that enmity, having ceased the law. And having come, he preached peace to you, both the far and the near. This shows that he does not call the law of Moses impious as if it were idolatry; for he says the idolaters are far, but the Jews are near. But the 'near' part shows piety and yet not perfection; for if they had perfection, they would not be near, but in it. And if they were again in opposition, they would not be near, but far away with the Greeks.

Here he wants to show that he did not cast [them] off as strangers and those taught by others, but that having been chosen as a preacher to the Gentiles, he owes [the revelation] to them also, and that just as the Lord taught those concerning John, so also I [do] according to revelation (Eph 3,2–3). But he felt that he was able to say something deeper, yet he measured his teaching to what they could contain.

So that it might be known now to the powers (Eph 3,10). Appropriately; for if it was hidden in God, all the powers were ignorant. For he does not speak of the present time, the time of grace, but from when the prophets began to reveal the things to come (Eph 3,15).

In the heavens, he says, is the conduct of the righteous, but on earth is that of all men (Eph 3,15); for the righteous are not arranged on the earth among the living, but are set apart like an exceptional race, those reclining with God. And it is said that the generation of these is heavenly as being pure, but the generation of the rest is earthly as being defiled. It should be noted that from which things the apostle shows the name of the Father, he did not ascend from us to the top, but came from above to us, making it clear that he is existing by nature and not by name only; for it is necessary always for the natural to be [followed by] the misuse, and of the natural first the...

english: From above, then from below. It should be noted, however, that he used the word 'patria' as if to signify kinship, not a formal clan; for everywhere the divine Scripture uses 'patria' to denote kinships.

He shaped it more typologically toward the type of the cross; for what else would the nature of depth, height, breadth, and length be if not that of the cross? And since he seems to speak of the cross as double, and not simply, but because the Lord's economy is divinity from above and humanity from below, and the apostolic preaching stretched from north to south and from east to west, gathering both the Lord's economy and the apostles' service, the doubling of the economy is thus demonstrated as being in a double cross; for it was not simply for him to name the places, the above and the below, and the line, the breadth and the length. 'That you may be filled into all the fullness of God' (Eph 3:18–19), which is the Church; for he says the Church is the fullness.

Regarding 'Awake, sleeper' (Eph 5:14), we find neither the old nor the new following it written anywhere. What then is it? It was then a gift, both of prayer and of psalms, being under the influence of the Spirit, just as he says to the Corinthians: 'each of you has a psalm, has a prayer.' What then is it? I will pray with the Spirit, I will pray also with the mind; I will sing a psalm with the Spirit, I will sing also with the mind; it is therefore evident that in one of these spiritual psalms, that is, prayers, lies that which he mentioned.

He who redeems a stranger's slave redeems and acquires him (Eph 5:29). Since the present time serves the evil ones, redeem him, so that he may be used for godliness (Eph 5:16). Since the Lamb was offered, and we eat his body. But food loves to be given back into the body of the eater—clearly [it is] spirit...

We visually eat his body. It is given to us for the body, and thus flesh from flesh, and bone from his bones. [Eph 5:32]. It is not the mystery, but God. What then is it that he says? That this formation of Adam and Eve, who was from him, and the connection has become a type of Christ and the church; through which he says: we are bone from his bones, and flesh from his flesh, just as Eve was from Adam. [Eph 5:32-33].

What I say regarding Christ and the church, he calls the mystery of marriage, instead of the type being according to the marriage law and the original creation of Christ and the church. For this reason he brought it forth: 'moreover you also, being one,' so that each man may love his own wife as himself. [Eph 5:31]. Why did he say 'being one'? Because the things according to Adam were a type of the church and of Christ. For this reason he said: 'and you also, each one love.' [Eph 5:33]. For the mystery of which marriage was a type has come to pass and is true, but the type itself must also be fulfilled, and each one love his own wife.

If the sword is the word of God, and the sword is of the Spirit, [Eph 6:17] then God is the Spirit of whom the sword is. If he said the Holy Spirit is the word of God, it is clear that just as the Son of God is the Word, so also the Spirit is the word of God. And he said the sword of the Spirit [is] the punitive energy of the Spirit.

'Praying in the Spirit,' [Eph 6:18] he did not say simply, but because we do not know how we ought to pray, he says elsewhere: the Spirit himself intercedes for us, so that these requests of ours may have nothing fleshly. But we have spiritual requests, being helped by the power of the Spirit.
Someone, he says, being delivered from corruption, that which is from the devil, receives in incorruption the grace of the Spirit. [Eph 6:24].
